incident-bot: Paging: SLO breach detected on continuous-batching path (us-west-2). p95=420ms, p99=1800ms, streaming stalls flagged for ~15m. Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming) and /v1/chat. Runbook: <https://intra.redwood/runbooks/cont-batch-latency|cont-batch-latency>

Maya: Acked, I'm on it. Seeing alerts + traces in dashboard. Will grab logs and check scheduler queues. @Devin can you confirm if this is only cont-batch or also standalone streaming workers? :eyes:

Devin: I'm on tail of the proxy and runtime logs now. Quick grab:
```
# runtimes/usw2/runner-17 logs
[14:08:02] batch_dispatch: avg_size=24 p95_size=40 p99_size=64
[14:08:03] tail_latency: active_streams=12 p99=2.1s tail_outliers=18
[14:08:04] kv_cache: evictions/sec=320 load=0.76
[14:08:05] scheduler: fairness_skew=0.44 heavy_long_sequences=7
```
Looks like batch sizes spiking and KV cache thrash. Stream stalls reported as token emission pauses (~2s) after first token.

Li: Noting that the mixed-seqlen jobs from model-alpha are high today (long-form summarization). Continuous batching is combining long and short seqs -> padding amplification. Also noticed high priority tenants flooding the high-throughput queue.

Alex: Adding data point from compile/kern logs — some kernels falling back to slower path for sequences >4096 tokens which increases per-token latency massively when mixed. If cont-batch entangles them with short seqs, short requests pay the penalty.

Maya: Customer impact assessment: initial estimate ~3.2% of requests in us-west-2 experienced visible stalls; 7 enterprise customers with streaming enabled may have partial streams. Sara, can you surface any support tickets?

Sara: I see 4 chat complaints mentioning stalls/dropped tokens in last 25m. I flagged two enterprise customers as high-touch and opened dedicated Slack DMs. I'll start templated outreach after we stabilize.

Devin: Proposed live mitigations (low-risk first):
- reduce CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE on us-west-2 cont-batch pool from 128 -> 32
- enable preemptive_shedding for long sequences so they don't hold head-of-queue
- temporarily disable continuous batching for streaming routes if improvement isn't immediate
Commands I'm going to use: 
```bash
redwoodctl rollout config set --pool cont-batch-usw2 --env CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=32
redwoodctl feature toggle set --pool cont-batch-usw2 preemptive_shedding=true
# if needed
redwoodctl feature toggle set --route /v1/generate continuous_batching=false
```

Maya: Sounds good. Please include canary on 10% of nodes first. Keep me posted.

Devin: Canary started at 14:16. Pushed CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=32 to 2/20 nodes. Observing metrics...

[14:22] Devin: Canary shows p95 down to 180ms, p99 down to 620ms on canary nodes. Overall cluster p99 still ~900ms due to remaining nodes. No errors in logs.

Alex: Nice. That points to config sensitivity. We should not need to fully disable cont-batch yet. Follow-up: need scheduler change to weight by seq_len (or prefer packing short-only batches). Filed infra ticket INFRA-4921.

Li: Rolling change to remaining nodes now with conservative ramp (3 nodes every 2m). Monitoring KV evictions and fairness_skew.

[14:28] incident-bot: Alert update: incident severity -> mitigated, SLO breach rate reduced to 0.6% cluster-wide. Continued monitoring for 30m.

Maya: Summary for handoff to next on-call (Jordan):
- What happened: continuous batching mixed long and short sequences, causing padding/kv thrash and amplifier effect on short requests -> streaming stalls and p99 spikes.
- Timeline: alerts at 14:05; canary rollback/config reduce at 14:16; cluster ramp 14:20-14:28; significant improvement by 14:22 on canary nodes.
- Actions taken: reduced CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE to 32 (canary -> full ramp), enabled preemptive_shedding, monitoring KV cache evictions, support outreach started for 7 affected customers.
- Outstanding work: scheduler fairness fix (INFRA-4921), longer-term option: seq_len-aware packing and kernel guardrails for >4k sequences. Postmortem owner: Alex.
- Mitigation rollback plan: if p99 regresses, set route /v1/generate continuous_batching=false for streaming-only path (hotfix).

Jordan: Taking handoff. I'll keep watch for the next 2 hours. If p99 creeps above 1s again I'll trigger route-level disable.

Maya: Thanks team. Sara, please send the templated message to the two enterprise customers acknowledging we investigated and will follow up.

Sara: On it, will send now and include the mitigation summary + ETA for follow-up call.

Devin: Leaving a small diagnostic dump here for post-incident debugging: 
```
# snapshot 14:30
cont-batch-usw2: nodes=20 avg_batch=22 p95=165 p99=590
kv_cache: hit=0.82 evict=110/s
scheduler: fairness_skew=0.10 (after ramp)
long_seq_count=3% traffic share
```

Alex: Notes for postmortem: examine model-alpha traffic patterns, see if model owner can patch to annotate long sequence requests so we can route them to a dedicated pool. Also evaluate auto-split for >4k tokens.

Maya: Logging handoff: I am off-call at 15:00. Jordan will own escalation. Please add any follow-ups to the incident Slack thread. :white_check_mark:

Jordan: Acknowledged. Monitoring dashboard pinned. Will notify if anything changes. :mag:

incident-bot: Incident closed -> monitoring watch for 30m. Final mitigation: CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=32, preemptive_shedding=true, scheduled INFRA-4921 for seq_len-aware scheduler.
